## Verdict in brief

1. **Gate 0.4(a): PASS, provisional; adopt the SoA compare kernel.** The candidate counts are
   [M]. Every timing is void as an A/B under plan §7 (foreign load above 10% or unrecorded, no
   interleaved repeats), so the PASS rests on the margin. In ID order, 32-entry SoA blocks with
   u8 lanes need 5.2-10.4x less CPU per tested candidate than today's layout in all 11 session
   x thread-count cells and on every request set, at least 1.3x above the 4x line. In pattern
   order they need 4.2-10.4x less on forward sets and 3.3-5.1x less on reverse checks per
   candidate. SoA-pattern's reverse ratio is undecided against 4x until a clean repeat. Per
   reverse request it needs 15.7-24x less CPU than today.
2. **Layout depends on the resolution rule [M].** First-found (epoch Rolling): SoA-pattern is
   best on real gen-7 streams (580 candidates per hit, 2,626 per miss, 2,938 per reverse check;
   SoA-id 910 / 3,902 / 9,999; today 1,134 / 4,585 / 12,330). Minimum-ID (legacy engine, W1.1
   strict Ordered identity, W2 canonical Lockstep): SoA in ID order; pattern ordering loses the
   min-ID early exit (6,720 candidates per hit vs 2,096 in ID order and 2,322 today).
3. **Gate 0.4(b): borderline and conditional [E]; W3.2 (miss path) moves into W2 as a
   conservative scope choice.** For the chosen design (pipeline + SoA-pattern first-found) the
   projected admission share of worker CPU is 6.3% at 74M. At N = 1G:
   - with one-thread costs and a uniform alpha 0.44-0.82 it is 16.8-35.0%. It crosses 25%
     only at alpha >= 0.65, and at 0.65 it is 24.8-27.4% across cost samples and MRU k, on the
     line;
   - with the layout's own miss and reverse thinning exponents it is 13.9-22.5% for a hit
     exponent of 0-0.69;
   - with the contaminated 48/90-thread factors on admission alone it is 23.9-58.2%;
   - with 90-thread factors on both admission and native work (x3.75) it is 9.6-26.2%.

   The trigger depends on two inputs that are not measured yet: the growth exponent by class
   at scale (no hit exponent exists for this layout) and clean thread factors. Misses plus
   reverse scans are 56% of the projected admission CPU at 74M, hits 38%.
4. **Gate 0.4(c): not triggered [M].** Cheap tiers resolve 76.6-88.9% of real gen-7 requests
   (MRU k = 1..64), 55.3-72.0% on C-5F and 73.2-98.7% on the four-loop runs.
5. **The replay is exact [M].** Rebuilding today's index in commit order reproduces every
   admission outcome, maintenance charge and retirement count of six traced runs (four-loop
   FG/BMW/H/X W6, FG W1, C-5F W18; 26,748,231 admissions, 0 mismatches), so `idxreplay` can
   serve as the differential oracle for the W1.1 kernel.

## Consequences for W1-W5 [E unless stated]

- **W1.1 kernel** (legacy lane, min-ID, strict Ordered identity): SoA blocks in ID order; the
  >= 4x per-candidate gate is met by SoA-id in every measured condition (provisional: the
  timings are void under §7, and the margin is at least 1.3x).
- **W2.3 inspector resolution**: layers in finite-upper-pattern order for first-found. The
  canonical Lockstep mode either keeps an ID-ordered copy or accepts about 2.5x CPU per hit on
  controls (57.6 vs 23.3 µs at one thread [M, timing void under §7]); a per-block minimum-ID
  skip in pattern order is untested. The W2.3 first-found vs canonical gate licenses
  first-found in production.
- **W2 gains W3.2** as a conservative scope choice under the borderline 0.4(b) projection: a
  sublinear structure for forward misses and reverse (retirement) scans (per-group dominance
  pruning on sorted lower corners, or the 2N+6 feature trie). Re-decide with the M-adm
  exponents by class on P-IMP and a clean thread sweep. If they project <= 25%, W3.2 can return
  to W3. Launch criterion (B) needs the same projection.
- **Route jobs** are 79% of jobs in the gen-7 window and 84.7% of their requests reach the
  layers (one request per job, no MRU/Local benefit) [M]: Route micro-batching (§3.4) matters
  for admission cost as well as for dispatch.
- **Snapshot refresh (A6)**: request-weighted stale share is 1.5% at a lag of 1,024 new IDs,
  2.6% at 65,536 and 3.5% at 1M [M, gen-7 streams]; the edge-based figures agree.
- **Measurement**: no timing here meets §7. The 48/90-thread sweep ran once, with 48 foreign
  busy CPUs during its 1-thread passes and 26-32 during the 48/90-thread passes. A clean repeat
  is still open: <= 10% foreign load, >= 2 interleaved repeats, v4 LoadMon fields and
  `schedstat`. It is the only way to settle the SoA-pattern reverse ratio against 4x and the
  thread factors that 0.4(b) depends on.

## 0.4 Method

1. **Static replay at gen 7** (`idxreplay static`): decodes all 74,156,033 domains, projects
   the tight summaries with an exact port of `power_domain/geometry.rs::project`, and loads the
   persisted candidate index. Self-checks on the fixture [M]: 0 signature mismatches over
   37,907,667 live IDs, 0 stored-envelope violations, 0 projection clamps, 0 summaries whose u8
   lanes saturate, 74,156,033 distinct raw images; lane test vs exact containment on 4.0M
   same-bucket pairs: 0 mismatches; AVX-512 kernels vs scalar reference on every block of the
   buckets of 200 queries at each thinning: 0 mismatched blocks.
   - Layouts: **l0-stored** = today's layout replicated type for type from the persisted
     blocks (ID-ordered 32-slot `[usize;32]` blocks, heap `Vec<AxisEnvelope>` envelopes, per-ID
     `bits: Vec<u64>` gather, `slots: Vec<u32>` into 176-byte `CompactSummary` slab entries);
     **l0-rebuilt** = the same with full blocks and exact envelopes; **soa-id** = 32-entry SoA
     blocks (u32 ids, u64 words, 36 u8 lanes field-major, block OR/AND words, u8 envelopes) in
     ID order; **soa-pattern** = the same ordered by finite-upper pattern then lexicographic
     lower corner (plan §3.3). Groups by signature are kept in all layouts.
   - Requests: miss proxies = 20,000 live IDs of the newest segment (self excluded; a live ID
     is maximal among live candidates); hit proxies = 10,000 retired, never-inspected IDs of
     gens 6-7 (every retired ID has a live container). Real streams: below.
   - Units: CPU ns per tested candidate (thread CPU clock / candidates evaluated; a SoA block
     counts its full length) and per bit test (word-only pass over the miss scan), candidates
     per hit (min-ID and first-found), per miss, per reverse check.
2. **Dynamic replay** (`idxreplay dynamic`) of traced complete runs: rebuilds today's index
   from scratch in the coordinator's commit order (`admit_with_lookup`, `find_controlled`,
   `maintenance_len`, `retire`, `insert`) and checks every admission's outcome and counters,
   then classifies every request of every inspection through the §3.2 pipeline.
3. **Real successor streams at 74M** (`idxreplay streams`): a traced resume of a gen-7 clone
   (`TMP/w0/intel/g7-trace-resume/`: trace binary edbe2729, W100 binding, Ready, v2 inputs,
   CPUs 128-227 under the socket-1 lock, 14:49-15:18Z, `elapsed_seconds` 1,722, cooperative
   stop, exit status 4 = paused, 0 frontiers, peak RSS 46.6 GB; natives 27,465,422 ->
   27,738,371 (+272,949), admitted domains 74,156,033 -> 75,033,320 (+877,287); its `run.log`
   "exit 0" is a script artefact, `stderr` records exit status 4). The replay loads the gen-7
   snapshot index, joins each traced inspection's post-cache event stream with the committed
   admission of each request, classifies every request through the §3.2 pipeline, and prices
   a sample of the layer-reaching requests (hits and misses, plus the reverse scan of each
   miss) on the three layouts. Containers admitted after the snapshot are counted separately
   (they would be stale misses of a gen-7 snapshot). The trace run is not a throughput
   baseline: about 1.4 busy native workers of 100, coordinator-bound, trace I/O, 51 foreign
   busy CPUs of 100 on socket 1 (recomputed from `socket1-load.txt`); only its request mix and
   counters are used.
4. **Stale-miss rate vs lag** (`idxreplay lag`): container age of every committed hit edge
   of all 1.19G gen-7 edges.

### Resolution pipeline on the traced complete runs (request-weighted, §3.2 order) [M]

Tiers: exact-job = image already requested by the same inspection (unbounded set; includes
today's KnownReuse), self = inside the inspected parent, local = inside an earlier miss of
the inspection, mru = inside one of the job's k most recent verified targets (same bucket),
exact-store = identical stored image older than the request, helper = pre-admitted orthant
reuse or inside an initial domain/orthant; the rest reach the layers (hit) or miss.

  rarely old low IDs, so the ID-order exit comes late for them. The real streams are the

## Gate 0.4(b): projected admission share at N = 1G [E]

Model (`tools/research/idxreplay/project.py`, grid driver `TMP/w0/intel/replay/gate04b.sh`,
outputs `replay/gate04b.txt`, `gate04b.jsonl`, full table `replay/t_gate04b.md`): admission CPU
per native at N domains is

  A(N) = r_hit c_hit f_hit s + r_miss (c_miss f_miss + c_rev f_rev) s + r_cheap c_cheap,
  s = (N / 74.16M)^alpha, share = A / (A + native CPU per native),

with, per native at MRU k=16 on the real gen-7 streams [M, `streams-g7-v4.jsonl`]: r_cheap
197.4, r_hit 25.02 layer hits, r_miss 3.21 misses (new domains), native 5.239 ms (wall of the
physical calls, used as CPU [E]); c = the measured one-thread CPU per request of each layout on
the sampled layer requests [M]; f = thread factor, per request set from the socket-1 sweep
(contaminated timing, see Threads) or 1; c_cheap = 100 ns per cheap-tier request [E, not
measured; 300 ns adds <= 0.7 points]. alpha is taken from the replay exponents
[M as fits, E as extrapolation]: 0.44 (static thinning, SoA-pattern candidates per miss),
0.65 (per-bucket regression, SoA-pattern), 0.69 / 0.73 (dynamic, C-5F hits / misses), 0.82
(dynamic maximum, four-loop H misses). "Today's engine" prices the engine's own forward-check
counters at today's per-candidate cost plus one today-layout reverse scan per new domain (no
pipeline). Assumptions [E]: the request mix per native of the traced window (79% Route jobs)
holds at 1G; live candidates grow in proportion to N; one alpha for all scanned classes (the
fix-round cells below relax this with `--class-alpha`); admission work runs on worker threads.
The multi-thread settings scale admission CPU by the thread factor but keep native CPU at
5.239 ms, the wall time of about 1.4 busy workers ("admission only"); only the native x3.75
setting scales both sides.

## Gate 0.4 verdict

- **0.4(a) kernel: PASS, provisional; adopt the SoA kernel.** The candidate counts are [M]. The
  timings are void under §7 in every session: 21% foreign load in the v4 streams run, 26-51
  foreign CPUs on socket 1, no receipt on CPUs 10-27, and no interleaved repeats. The PASS rests
  on the margin. In ID order SoA blocks need 5.2-10.4x less CPU per tested candidate than
  today's layout in all 11 session x thread-count cells (5 processes, widely varying load) and
  on every request set: 1 thread static 5.4-10.4x over three sessions, 7.9-9.5x in the first
  stats pass; real streams 6.6-9.6x; 18 threads 7.0-7.9x; 48/90 threads 5.2-7.8x. The minimum is
  1.3x above the 4x line. In pattern order they need 4.2-10.4x less on the forward sets
  everywhere. On reverse checks pattern order needs 3.3-5.1x less per tested candidate and
  falls below 4x in three cells that are no more contaminated than the others, so SoA-pattern's
  reverse ratio against 4x is **undecided** until a clean repeat. Per reverse request, pattern
  order is still the cheapest layout (15.7-24x less CPU than today; its candidate counts are
  [M]).
- **Layout choice (by candidates per hit and per miss on real streams) [M]:**
  - First-found (the epoch engine's production Rolling resolution, "first verified container
    wins"): **SoA-pattern** (580 candidates per hit, 2,626 per miss, 2,938 per reverse check vs
    SoA-id 910 / 3,902 / 9,999 and today 1,134 / 4,585 / 12,330).
  - Minimum-ID (the legacy engine's rule, the W1.1 legacy-lane kernel with strict Ordered
    identity, and the W2 canonical Lockstep oracle): **SoA in ID order**. Pattern ordering loses
    the min-ID early exit: 6,720 candidates per hit vs 2,096 in ID order (2.5x the CPU per hit).
  - Consequence [E]: the W1.1 kernel on the legacy lane keeps ID order; the epoch layers use
    pattern order for first-found resolution. If the canonical mode must also run at scale (not
    only on controls), either keep an ID-ordered copy of the layers or add a per-block minimum-ID
    skip to the pattern-ordered scan (not measured). The W2.3 gate (first-found vs canonical
    natives within +-5%, edges within +-10%) is what licenses first-found in production.
- **0.4(b) miss path: borderline and conditional [E]. W3.2 moves into W2 as a conservative
  scope choice, not as a clean trigger.** For the chosen design (pipeline + SoA-pattern
  first-found) the projected admission share at N = 1G:
  - exceeds 25% at 1-thread costs only for a uniform alpha >= 0.65. At 0.65 it is 24.8-27.4%
    across the k=16/64 and cost-sample variants, on the line;
  - exceeds 25% at nearly every exponent with the contaminated 48/90-thread factors applied to
    admission alone (native kept at the 1.4-worker wall time);
  - stays below 25% at SoA-pattern's own thinning exponents for misses and reverse scans at one
    thread (13.9-22.5% for a hit exponent of 0-0.69);
  - stays below 25% when native CPU is scaled by the same gate-0.3 in-process contention
    (x3.75) for alpha <= 0.73 (it reaches 26.2% at 0.82).

  The uniform alphas 0.65-0.82 are a per-bucket cross-section (0.65) and dynamic exponents of
  today's layout on small growing walks (0.69-0.82). They are not measurements of the chosen
  layout at scale. Moving W3.2 into W2 keeps the option of meeting launch criterion (B)
  ("projected admission share at N = 1G <= 25%, from the exponent") without a late redesign.
  Scope it on reverse scans as well as forward misses (together 56% of the projected admission
  CPU at 74M). Re-decide with the M-adm exponents by class (hits, misses, reverse) on P-IMP and
  a clean thread sweep. If those project <= 25%, W3.2 can return to W3.
- **0.4(c) pipeline: not triggered [M].** The cheap tiers resolve 76.6-88.9% of real gen-7
  requests (k = 1..64), 55.3-72.0% on C-5F and 73.2-98.7% on the four-loop runs, all >= 50%,
  so §3.2 needs no redesign. Route jobs are the exception inside the mix (10.1% cheap, 84.7%
  layer hits on gen-7 streams): Route micro-batching (§3.4) is the lever for them.
- **Plan item 0.4 "1/48/90 threads": incomplete.** It was measured once, with 48.1 foreign busy
  CPUs during the 1-thread passes and 31.9 / 26.1 during the 48 / 90-thread passes, on a
  saturated socket at 90 threads. It does not meet the §7 protocol (>= 2 interleaved repeats,
  <= 10% foreign load, `schedstat`). Counts are valid. The thread factors enter the projection
  only as a contaminated sensitivity, and the direction of their bias is unknown.

## Open issues

1. Every timing is void under §7, and the 48/90-thread sweep is a single contaminated pass. A
   clean repeat needs a socket-1 window with <= 10% foreign load, >= 2 interleaved repeats, the
   v4 LoadMon fields (`foreign_busy_own_cpus` and `busy_smt_siblings` in every
   `stats`/`throughput` row) and `schedstat` run delay. Such a window is not available while
   `nfink`'s gammaboard/postgres jobs float over all CPUs: 53.7 of 100 CPUs on 128-227 were busy
   at 20:23Z, and `socket1.lock` was held and queued by other lanes
   (`socket1-lockstate-2026-09-27T2023Z.txt`). Until then the SoA-pattern reverse ratio
   (3.3-5.1x; below 4x at 1 thread in the lane-18 stats pass and at 48/90 threads) is undecided
   against the 4x line. The thread factors (2.0-2.9x at 90 threads) are biased in an unknown
   direction.
2. The projection's alpha is an extrapolation from 74M to 1G by a factor of 13.5. The fits come
   from thinning one snapshot (misses and reverse scans only, 0.44-0.50 for SoA-pattern), from
   a per-bucket cross-section (0.65), or from small growing walks with today's layout
   (0.69-0.82). No hit exponent exists for the chosen layout: thinned hit proxies lose their
   containers (found fraction 0.31 at 25% live). Gate 0.4(b) turns on these inputs. Measure the
   exponent by class (hit, miss, reverse) on P-IMP and P-FRESH (M-adm) before sizing W3.2 or
   moving it back to W3.
3. c_cheap (100 ns per cheap-tier request) is not measured; the epoch engine's exact-job set,
   MRU and Local tests need a micro-benchmark (the sensitivity at 300 ns is <= 0.7 points).
4. Native time per job is the physical-call wall time of a traced run with about 1.4 busy
   workers under foreign load; at 90 inspectors the native CPU per native changes (gate 0.3:
   3.75x at K=96 in one process). The projection shows both ends; the epoch design decision on
   inspector processes (W0.3) moves the share accordingly.
5. The real-stream layer costs use the static gen-7 snapshot index, not an evolving one;
   3.7% of the window's hits target post-snapshot containers and are reported separately.
   80 jobs (46,947 event records) could not be joined and are skipped. The layer-cost sampler
   is not deterministic run to run. Two samples agree within 2.3% on candidates, but they
   differ by 8.5% in projected admission CPU (0.351 vs 0.381 ms per native), which moves the
   alpha-0.65 share between 25.8% and 27.4%.
6. The traced resume is W100 Ready on 128-227 but only about 1.4 native workers were busy
   (coordinator-bound, 6.7 GB coordinator trace); its request mix is 79% Route jobs by count.
   A mix drawn from an inspection-bound engine could differ.
7. C-5F was traced at W18 on CPUs 10-27, not at the plan's W50.
8. Pattern-order min-ID: a per-block minimum-ID skip (continue past blocks whose minimum ID
   exceeds the best found) is not implemented in `soa.rs` for pattern order; its effect on the
   6,720 candidates per hit is unmeasured.
9. `rtool cover/union`, `meas/fits.py` and `membench` were not re-run against their committed
   outputs (W0.1 reproduction covers `scan2`, `indexscan`, `deg`).
10. Cleanup once the results are frozen: `.claude/worktrees/fable51-py/TMP/gen7-resume` was
    mutated by the traced resume (CP5 generation 9) and must not be used as a gen-7 fixture;
    the trace directories (`g7-trace-resume/trace` 12 GB logical, `trace-5f` ~5 GB) can go once
    no lane needs them. `TMP/gen7` stays read-only (file list, sizes and manifests identical to
    `TMP/v2-checkpoint-copy-gen7`, checked 19:53Z).
